Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, I'm so worried about his eyesight. He sits way too close to the TV when watching cartoons and also when reading books. I've tried to get him to move back a bit, but he says he can't see as well then.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Sometimes I call his name and he doesn't respond right away. It's like he's not hearing me or maybe just ignoring me? But if I go over to him and say it again، he'll usually answer. I don't know if it's his hearing or just him being a bit distracted.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teeth are a worry for me because the dentist said the enamel is weak. We have to be super careful with sugary foods and make sure he brushes them really well to prevent cavities.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: When he plays outside with friends， his breathing gets much faster than the other kids. Even when they're all running around together， my son seems to be panting more. I've mentioned it to his dad， but we haven't done anything about it yet.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Poor baby... he has low muscle tone. The physiotherapist is working with him to improve it. You can see it when he walks or tries to hold things; it's just a bit more effortful for him than for other kids his age.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Eating can be tricky sometimes. He's super fussy about food textures and won't eat certain things because of how they feel in his mouth. Like， mashed potatoes are okay but not if they're lumpy at all.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Yes... his fingers are shorter than usual. We were told it's just something he was born with and doesn't affect anything else.

    - Children with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing autoimmune diseases, particularly inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and type 1 diabetes. a) How this affects the patient:

a) How this affects the patient:

    - Children with KBG syndrome may experience various skin conditions, including eczema, keratosis pilaris, and hirsutism (increased body hair). The presence of synophrys (joined eyebrows) can contribute to a unique facial appearance.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our son has mentioned having trouble seeing the board at school, especially when the teacher writes in small letters or from a distance. We've noticed he squints or leans forward to get a better look.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: He tends to turn the volume of the TV very high, even when we ask him to lower it. This makes us wonder if he's having some difficulty hearing, though he doesn't seem to have trouble understanding us when we speak directly to him.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Chewing harder foods like meat or crunchy vegetables is a challenge for him. He often avoids those foods or asks for them to be cut into smaller pieces, which makes mealtime a bit more complicated.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: During physical activities like running or playing sports, he can't seem to keep up with his peers for very long. He gets tired easily and sometimes needs to sit down and rest, which is concerning because he's otherwise an active boy who loves to play outside.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Yes, there have been episodes where he stares off into space and doesn't respond immediately when we call his name. These episodes are brief but unsettling, and we're not sure what causes them or how to respond appropriately.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: His weight gain has been slower compared to his peers. He eats well and has a good appetite, but just doesn't seem to be putting on weight as quickly as other children his age.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: He was diagnosed with hip dysplasia, which required some monitoring and physiotherapy to ensure proper development and prevent future complications. We're diligent about his follow-up appointments to keep track of his progress.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome may experience respiratory issues, such as recurrent otitis media (middle ear infections) and temporary blockage of the Eustachian tubes (glue ear). These can lead to hearing difficulties and temporary hearing loss, which may require treatment with antibiotics or hearing aids.
    
## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of congenital heart defects, specifically valve abnormalities and holes in the heart chambers. Regular cardiovascular assessments are recommended to monitor for potential issues.
    
## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties and swallowing issues, leading to a preference for softer textures and avoiding certain foods. They may also develop gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), characterized by frequent regurgitation and discomfort after meals.
    
## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Individuals with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing autoimmune diseases, particularly inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and type 1 diabetes. Regular immunological screenings and monitoring are advised.
    
## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Neurological features in KBG syndrome include developmental delays, behavioral differences, and occasional seizures. Management strategies should focus on addressing these specific challenges.
    
## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are prone to recurrent otitis media (ear infections) and glue ear (build-up of fluid in the ear), requiring timely intervention with antibiotics and possible grommet insertion.
    
## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Vision-related concerns in KBG syndrome include refractive errors (such as nearsightedness, farsightedness, and astigmatism), strabismus (eye misalignment), and presbyopia (difficulty reading close-up). Regular eye examinations are crucial for monitoring and managing these issues.
    
## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Individuals with KBG syndrome may exhibit skin concerns such as eczema-like patches, hyperpigmentation, and thinning of the skin. Dermatological evaluations should be conducted to address these issues.
    
## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Dental concerns in KBG syndrome include weak enamel, susceptibility to tooth decay, and orthodontic issues such as bruxism (teeth grinding) and malocclusion (misaligned teeth). Regular dental check-ups are essential.

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

An Individualized Education Plan (IEP) tailored to their unique needs should be implemented.

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

    - Behavioural differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety, are common in KBG syndrome. Early identification and appropriate interventions are critical for supporting emotional and social development.

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

    - Skeletal features in KBG syndrome include brachydactylism (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth finger). Monitoring for skeletal anomalies, particularly those affecting the spine (scoliosis) and hips (hip dysplasia), is essential.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience respiratory issues, including recurrent otitis media (middle ear infections) and temporary enlargement of the tonsils (tonsillar hypertrophy).

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of congenital heart defects, specifically valve abnormalities and septal defects. They are also more prone to developing heart-related complications, such as arrhythmias and cardiomyopathies.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), leading to poor weight gain and nutritional deficiencies. They may also develop vitamin D deficiency rickets due to impaired calcium absorption.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to autoimmune diseases and inflammatory conditions, such as Type 1 diabetes, autoimmune thyroiditis, and lupus-like conditions. They may also be at an increased risk of developing autoimmune reactions to vaccines.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Hypotonia (low muscle tone) is a common feature in KBG syndrome, affecting balance, coordination, and strength. Children may struggle with fine motor skills, such as buttoning clothes or picking up small objects, and may require adaptations in their home and school environments.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Neurodevelopmental delays are a hallmark of KBG syndrome, characterized by cognitive impairment, behavioral differences, and challenges in social interaction. Management strategies should focus on compensatory strategies and assistive devices to enhance functional abilities.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to otitis media (ear infections) and adenovirus-induced pneumonia. Regular ENT (Ear, Nose, Throat) surveillance is recommended to detect potential issues early.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- Myopia (nearsightedness) is a common ocular issue in KBG syndrome, contributing to difficulty focusing on distant objects and requiring corrective lenses.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Vision problems, particularly refractive errors, are frequent in KBG syndrome. Regular eye examinations are essential to monitor progression and adjust spectacles as needed.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Synophrys (joined eyebrows) and microcephaly (smaller-than-average brain size) are notable facial features associated with KBG syndrome.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- The characteristic facial appearance, including synophrys and microcephaly, is a defining feature of KBG syndrome and can impact self-esteem and social interactions.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- Macrodontia of the upper central incisors (large molars) and susceptibility to tooth decay are common dental concerns in KBG syndrome.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Teeth sensitivity and possible enamel thinning increase the risk of cavities and other dental issues, necessitating thorough oral hygiene practices and regular dental visits.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Education needs vary widely among individuals with KBG syndrome. While many achieve success in mainstream settings, those with significant learning difficulties may require additional support in the classroom. Special educational provision (such as Individual Education Plans [IEPs] or EHCPs) should be considered based on individual needs.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- Behavioural differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, and anxiety, are common in KBG syndrome. Management strategies should focus on behavior modification techniques, sensory integration therapies, and targeted educational programs.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- The presence of behavioral differences impacts social interactions, emotional regulation, and overall quality of life. Early intervention and consistent support are crucial for managing these challenges.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- Brachydactyly (shortened fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth finger) are characteristic features of KBG syndrome. These can lead to difficulties with grooming and potentially contribute to orthopedic concerns.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Skeletal anomalies, such as brachydactyly and clinodactyly, can influence hand and foot morphology, potentially impacting dexterity and comfort during play and daily activities.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS

a) Screening:
- Regular dental check-ups and orthodontic evaluations.
- Monitoring for cardiovascular issues, including echocardiograms and ECGs.
- Surveillance for hearing concerns, including audiometric testing.
- Review for cranial vault and facial measurements to assess for anomalies.
- Orthopedic evaluation for skeletal features and musculoskeletal flexibility.

b) Treatments:
- Speech therapy to address communication and swallowing difficulties.
- Occupational therapy to improve fine motor skills and ADLs.
- Physical therapy to address muscle tone and mobility.
- Behavioral therapy to address behavioral differences and ASD characteristics.
- Nutritional support, including Vitamin D supplementation, to prevent rickets.
- Anticonvulsants for seizure management.
- Thyroid hormone replacement therapy for hypothyroidism.
- Antibiotics for recurrent otitis media.
- Immunizations according to local guidelines.

This comprehensive approach addresses the unique medical, developmental, and behavioral aspects of KBG syndrome, providing tailored recommendations for screening, treatment, and management. Regular reassessment and adjustment of interventions based on the evolving needs of the individual patient is paramount.

a) How this affects the patient:

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience respiratory issues, including recurrent otitis media (middle ear infections) and temporary blockage of the Eustachian tubes (glue ear). These can lead to temporary hearing loss and contribute to sleep disturbances and behavioral issues.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular ENT (Ear, Nose, Throat) review.
  - Addressing sleep apnea (if present).

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at increased risk of congenital heart defects, particularly valve abnormalities and septal defects (holes between the heart chambers). These can result in various symptoms, including persistent cyanosis (blue-tinted skin), clubbing of the fingers, and irregular heartbeat (arrhythmias).
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular echocardiogram review.
  - Cardiac evaluation as per clinical judgment based on additional symptoms or family history.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties, including refusal to try new foods, picky eating, and texture discrimination (tasting and rejecting unfamiliar textures). These can lead to nutritional deficiencies and delays in reaching developmental milestones.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Feeding therapy (e.g., PNF techniques, taste discrimination training).
  - Nutritional assessment and supplementation as indicated.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at increased risk of developing autoimmune diseases, particularly Type 1 diabetes mellitus and inflammatory bowel disease. They are also more susceptible to fungal and viral infections.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Immunological surveillance and prophylactic antibiotics as advised by immunologist.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome frequently exhibit neurodevelopmental features, including learning difficulties, behavioral differences, and sensorineural hearing loss. They may also demonstrate autistic-like behaviors and social communication challenges.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Speech therapy and behavioral intervention.
  - Educational support and accommodations as needed.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are prone to recurrent otitis media (ear infections) and glue ear (build-up of fluid in the ear), leading to hearing difficulties and sleep disturbances.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular ENT review.
  - Monitoring and treating glue ear with ventilation tubes (grommets) as needed.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at increased risk of vision-related issues, including refractive errors (short-sightedness, far-sightedness, astigmatism), squint (strabismus), and presbyopia (difficulty reading in old age).
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular ophthalmology review.
  - Orthokeratology (corneal contact lenses) for near-sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may develop eczema (atopic dermatitis) and other skin conditions, particularly affecting the scalp and nails.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Skeletally, children with KBG syndrome may experience developmental delay, specifically in areas such as fine motor skills (using utensils, tying shoelaces), gross motor skills (walking, running), and coordination.

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent respiratory infections, particularly in the first year of life.
  
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Common occurrence of respiratory tract infections, particularly in young children.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- No mention of cardiovascular issues.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Possible presence of congenital heart defects, but none were noted in this patient.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Difficulty swallowing (dysphagia) and feeding challenges.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Feeding difficulties and potential gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- No mention of immunological issues.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Potential susceptibility to autoimmune diseases.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Neurological issues affecting brain development and function.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Brain anomalies and possible cognitive delays.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

- Frequent ear infections and hearing issues.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Common occurrence of otitis media and sensorineural hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient:
- Vision problems such as astigmatism and short-sightedness (hypermetropia).

- Possible presence of dermatological abnormalities.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Dental issues, including weak enamel and potential orthodontic concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- Need for additional educational support and accommodations.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Potential for academic challenges and behavioral differences.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent respiratory infections, including pneumonia and bronchiolitis.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Common among individuals with KBG syndrome due to the presence of the ANKRD11 gene variant.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- None noted.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Heart conditions are relatively common in individuals with KBG syndrome, including valve abnormalities and congenital heart defects.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Difficulty swallowing (dysphagia) and feeding issues.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Feeding difficulties and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) are commonly reported in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Susceptibility to infections and autoimmune diseases.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing autoimmune conditions and infections.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Epilepsy requiring medication.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Neurological conditions affecting movement, coordination, and cognitive functions are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- Fluid buildup in the ears (otitis media) and nasal blockages.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Nasal blockages and fluid buildup in the ears are frequent complaints in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- Vision problems such as astigmatism and short-sightedness (myopia).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Vision-related issues are common in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the presence of the ANKRD11 gene variant.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Skin conditions such as eczema and keratosis pilaris.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Skin conditions are not unique to individuals with KBG syndrome but are more common in this population.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- Difficulties chewing and managing tooth decay.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Dental issues are common in individuals with KBG syndrome due to the presence of the ANKRD11 gene variant.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- Need for additional educational support and accommodations.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome typically require additional support in school, particularly with respect to physical needs and behavioral differences.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- Behavioral differences, autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and learning difficulties.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioral differences, ASD, and learning difficulties are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- An unusual structure of the spinal bones (scoliosis) and short fingers (brachydactyly).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of the spinal bones (scoliosis) and short fingers (brachydactyly), are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
- Regular dental check-ups.
- Monitoring for heart conditions (echocardiogram and ECG).
- Management of epilepsy.
- Monitoring for digestive issues (stool frequency, consistency, and odor).
- Monitoring for vision issues (regular eye exams).
- Monitoring for neurological issues (EEG, brain MRI, and developmental assessments).
- Monitoring for immune system issues (vaccination schedule and antibody testing).
- Monitoring for gastrointestinal issues (bowel motility and stool characteristics).
- Monitoring for cardiovascular issues (follow-up echocardiograms and ECGs).
- Monitoring for orthopedic issues (physical therapy and exercise program).
- Monitoring for neurodevelopmental outcomes (speech, fine motor skills, and cognitive abilities).
- Monitoring for behavioral outcomes (ADHD, autism spectrum traits, and social-emotional development).
- Consideration of immunotherapy options for recurrent infections and autoimmune conditions.
- Consideration of dietary modifications and supplements (calcium, vitamin D, omega-3 fatty acids) based on nutritional assessment.
- Consideration of physical activity programs tailored to individual capabilities.
- Consideration of educational interventions (specialized curriculum, behavior modification strategies, and assistive technology).
- Consideration of psychological support and counseling services.
- Consideration of peer groups and social opportunities.
- Consideration of future medical advancements and potential therapies (gene editing, CRISPR-based approaches, etc.).

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent respiratory infections, including pneumonia and bronchiolitis.
  
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Common occurrence of respiratory tract infections, particularly in infants and young children.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- No congenital heart defects were noted during the physical examination.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Congenital heart defects are uncommon in KBG syndrome, occurring in approximately 10-20% of affected individuals.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent gastrointestinal issues, including reflux, constipation, and food intolerances.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- GI disturbances are relatively common in KBG syndrome, affecting approximately 70-80% of affected individuals.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Susceptibility to viral infections, particularly respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Increased susceptibility to viral infections is a hallmark of KBG syndrome.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent seizures, ranging from minor focal seizures to more complex generalized tonic-clonic seizures.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Seizure frequency and severity are commonly reported in KBG syndrome.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent ear infections, including mastoiditis.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Ear infections are a frequent complication in KBG syndrome, potentially due to anatomical variations.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- Vision-related issues, including refractive errors and strabismus.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Vision problems are common in KBG syndrome, affecting approximately 70-80% of affected individuals.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- No dermatological issues were noted during the consultation.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- No specific dermatological concerns were reported.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent dental issues, including caries and orthodontic concerns.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Dental issues are common in KBG syndrome, affecting approximately 70-80% of affected individuals.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- Limited academic achievement, requiring additional educational support.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Academic challenges are a common feature of KBG syndrome, affecting approximately 70-80% of affected individuals.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- Behavioral and developmental delays, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioral and developmental challenges are a hallmark of KBG syndrome, affecting approximately 70-80% of affected individuals.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- Anomalies of the spine (scoliosis) and short fingers (brachydactyly).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Skeletal anomalies are a common feature of KBG syndrome, affecting approximately 70-80% of affected individuals.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
- Regular dental check-ups.
- Monitoring for scoliosis and brachydactyly.
- Considering a cardiovascular review following diagnosis.
- Monitoring for tethered cord (MRI) if sacral dimple is present.
- Referral for a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) following diagnosis.
- Consider a gastroenterology review for digestive issues.
- Consider behavioral therapy and educational support.
- Follow-up immunizations and vaccinations as recommended by the healthcare provider.
- Monitor seizure frequency and response to treatment.
- Consider neurodevelopmental assessments and interventions as needed.
- Review and address vision concerns, including regular eye checks and consideration of spectacles.
- Monitor hearing concerns and refer for further evaluation if necessary.
- Consider orthodontic review for dental issues.
- Monitor and address gastrointestinal concerns, including dietary management and review of feeding issues.
- Consider psychological support and counseling as needed.
- Monitor and address neurological concerns, including seizure management and orthopedic review.
- Consider genetic testing and surveillance for potential future health concerns.

## 1) RESPIRATORY

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome may experience respiratory issues, including recurrent otitis media (middle ear infections) and temporary nasal blockages. Proper hygiene practices and timely antibiotic treatment can reduce the frequency of these infections.
    
## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of congenital heart defects, specifically valve abnormalities and septal defects. Regular echocardiograms and follow-up with a pediatric cardiologist are recommended.
    
## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). Management strategies such as gradual introduction of solid foods, dietary modifications, and antacid medications may alleviate symptoms.
    
## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Individuals with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of developing autoimmune diseases, particularly Type 1 diabetes mellitus. Routine immunological screening and consideration of prophylactic vaccinations are advised.
    
## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome frequently exhibit developmental delays, behavioral differences, and sensorineural hearing loss. Speech therapy and educational interventions are crucial components of management.
    
## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are prone to recurrent otitis media (middle ear infections) and temporary nasal blockages. Proper hygiene practices and timely antibiotic treatment can reduce the frequency of these infections.
    
## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of vision-related issues, including refractive errors (short-sightedness, far-sightedness, and astigmatism) and strabismus (eye misalignment). Regular eye examinations are essential for early detection and intervention.
    
## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome may display eczema-like skin conditions, particularly affecting the scalp and intertriginous areas (areas between folds of skin). Gentle cleansing techniques and avoidance of irritants are key management strategies.
    
## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are susceptible to tooth decay (dental caries) due to their weak enamel and frequent bottle-feeding habits. Regular dental check-ups and thorough cleaning routines are vital.
    
## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Education outcomes for individuals with KBG syndrome vary widely. While many achieve success in mainstream education, those with significant learning challenges may require additional support in special educational environments.
    
## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Behavioural differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety, are common in individuals with KBG syndrome. Early identification and appropriate therapeutic interventions are critical.
    
## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome frequently experience skeletal anomalies, such as brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth finger). Orthodontic and orthopedic evaluations are advisable.
    
## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Regular dental check-ups: Given the high incidence of dental issues, routine dental visits are essential.
b) Regular hearing assessments: Monitoring hearing thresholds helps identify potential hearing loss early.
c) Vision screenings: Frequent eye exams are crucial to detect and address refractive errors and other vision problems.
d) Cardiac evaluation: Following diagnosis, periodic cardiac evaluations are necessary to rule out underlying heart conditions.
e) Skeletal assessment: X-rays of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull should be conducted to evaluate bone maturity and assess for possible skeletal anomalies.
f) Dental care: Implement proper oral hygiene practices and consult a pediatric dentist for guidance.
g) Immunizations: Administer vaccines according to public health protocols to prevent infectious diseases.
h) Speech therapy: Engage in speech therapy programs to aid communication and improve articulation.
i) Behavioral therapy: Introduce behavior modification techniques to address challenging behaviors.
j) Nutritional counseling: Consult with a nutritionist to develop a balanced diet tailored to the child's needs.
k) Physical therapy: Incorporate physical therapy sessions to enhance coordination and strength.

m) Speech therapy: Participate in speech therapy programs to address speech delays and refine vocalization.
n) Genetic counseling: Discuss options for carrier testing and prenatal testing with a genetic counselor.
o) Follow-up appointments: Schedule regular follow-up appointments with specialists to monitor progress and adjust management plans as needed.
p) Medical surveillance: Conduct annual thyroid function tests and consider monitoring for other endocrine imbalances.
q) Vaccinations: Maintain current vaccination schedules per local guidelines.
r) Epilepsy management: Review seizure control measures and consider medication adjustments as necessary.
s) Vestibular rehabilitation: Evaluate and potentially implement vestibular therapy to address balance and dizziness concerns.
t) Palatal evaluation: Refer for a palate review if persistent feeding difficulties or speech concerns persist.
u) Tethered cord evaluation: Consider MRI scans for infants with asymmetrical hip creases or asymmetric gait.
v) Growth monitoring: Regularly track height and weight percentile status and refer for further investigation if deviations from the expected range are noted.
w) Hormone replacement: Evaluate the need for supplemental hormones based on laboratory results and clinical observations.
x) Gluten-free/dietary evaluation: Explore gluten-free diets under supervision to investigate potential gut sensitivity.
y) Vitamin D supplementation: Assess vitamin D levels and consider supplementation if deficient.
z) Sleep apnea evaluation: Investigate sleep patterns and consider CPAP therapy if necessary.
aa) Additional considerations: Monitor for signs of tethered cord syndrome and consider MRI scans for infants with sacral dimple and asymmetrical gait.

consultation:
Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Honestly, I'm worried about his eyesight. He complains that things look blurry sometimes, and it's hard to know if it's just a phase or something more serious. I've noticed he squints or rubs his eyes frequently.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes... he seems to have trouble hearing certain sounds. Like, when we're watching TV, he'll ask us to turn it up because he can't hear it well. It's concerning because he should be able to pick up on conversations and shows easily at his age.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Chewing has become a challenge for him lately. Harder foods like apples or meat are difficult for him to manage. We've had to adjust his diet somewhat to softer foods to make mealtime less stressful.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Physical activity... he just can't seem to keep up with the other kids. Even simple games like tag or running around leave him winded and tired quickly. It worries me that there might be an underlying issue we need to address.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: The tethered cord issue is something we're closely monitoring. The specialists have assured us they're on top of it, but it's still a concern for us as parents.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Mealtime... it's often a struggle. He has days where eating is just really hard for him. The food either doesn't agree with him or he's just not interested. We try to keep a routine and offer a variety of foods to see what works best for him.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Well... aside from what we've discussed, his movements are slightly different from his peers. And he was diagnosed with scoliosis. These are things we're working through with his therapists and doctors to ensure he gets the right support and care.

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome may experience respiratory issues, including recurrent ear infections and temporary loss of smell (anosmia). Proper hygiene practices and timely antibiotic treatment can reduce the frequency of these complications.
    
## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are at increased risk of congenital heart defects, particularly valve abnormalities. Regular echocardiograms and follow-up with a pediatric cardiologist are recommended to monitor for potential issues.
    
## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties and swallowing issues. They may require dietary modifications and therapeutic feeding tubes (PEG or GES) for prolonged periods. Speech therapy and gastroenterological evaluations are crucial for managing these challenges.
    
## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Individuals with KBG syndrome are at increased risk of developing autoimmune diseases, particularly Type 1 diabetes and thyroid disorders. Regular screening and immunotherapy may be considered depending on the presence of autoantibodies.
    
## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome frequently exhibit developmental delays, behavioral differences, and learning difficulties. Management strategies involving physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and educational support are essential components of their care plan.
    
## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are prone to recurrent ear infections (otitis media) and glue ear (fluid in the ear). Regular audiometric testing and consideration of hearing aid placement are advisable. Nasal congestion and sinus issues are common and may necessitate nasal spray treatments and occasional antibiotics.
    
## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Vision-related concerns in KBG syndrome include refractive errors (such as nearsightedness, farsightedness, and astigmatism), strabismus (eye misalignment), and presbyopia (difficulty reading close-up). Regular ophthalmologic examinations are critical for monitoring and addressing these issues.
    
## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Individuals with KBG syndrome may display eczema-like skin conditions, including dry, itchy patches that can be stubborn to treat. Frequent bathing, gentle skincare routines, and avoiding harsh chemicals are key considerations.

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

a) How this affects the patient:

a) How this affects the patient:

Features include autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), anxiety, and sensory integration dysfunction. # CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience respiratory issues, including recurrent otitis media (middle ear infections) and temporary enlargement of the tonsils (tonsillar hypertrophy).

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of congenital heart defects, specifically valve abnormalities and septal defects. They are also more prone to developing heart-related complications, such as arrhythmias and cardiomyopathy.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties and swallowing issues, leading to a preference for softer foods. They may also develop gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and constipation.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to autoimmune diseases and inflammatory conditions, such as Type 1 diabetes, autoimmune thyroiditis, and lupus-like conditions.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome frequently exhibit developmental delays, behavioral differences, and learning difficulties. They may also display autistic traits, such as social awkwardness and repetitive behaviors.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are more prone to developing otitis media (ear infections) and adenotonsillar hypertrophy (enlargement of the lymph nodes in the throat), which can lead to difficulty breathing and sleep apnea.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of strabismus (eye misalignment) and amblyopia (lazy eye), which can impact depth perception and visual acuity.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience eczema and skin tags, particularly on the tongue and lips.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are more likely to experience tooth decay (dental caries) and bruxism (teeth grinding) due to the enlarged size of their molars.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Education outcomes for children with KBG syndrome vary widely. While many achieve success in mainstream education, those with more significant learning challenges may require additional support and accommodations.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioural differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD) characteristics, have been reported in many affected individuals. Learning difficulties and developmental delays are also common.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome frequently exhibit skeletal anomalies, such as brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth finger). An increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis) is also a noted feature.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
### Screening Recommendations:
- Regular dental check-ups: Monitoring for potential issues such as tooth decay and gum inflammation.
- Hearing screenings: Routine audiometric evaluations to address hearing impairments and assess the effectiveness of hearing aid use.
- Vision screening: Periodic ophthalmological examinations to detect and address refractive errors and ocular health concerns.
- Cardiac surveillance: Follow-up echocardiograms and EKGs to monitor for potential heart conditions and track the progression of existing heart issues.
- Orthopedic evaluation: Considering a skeletal survey (X-rays of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to evaluate bone maturity and rule out developmental dyschondroblastoma, a benign tumor affecting growing bones.

### Treatments Recommendations:
- Speech therapy: Addressing communication and language delays associated with KBG syndrome.
- Behavioral therapy: Supporting emotional regulation and social interaction.
- Physical therapy: Enhancing fine motor skills and coordination.
- Occupational therapy: Improving self-care abilities and daily living skills.
- Nutritional counseling: Ensuring adequate caloric intake and proper nutrition to support overall growth and development.
- Anticonvulsants: Managing seizure activity, especially if present.
- Hearing aids: Treating conductive hearing loss, if present.
- Dental care: Implementing a comprehensive oral hygiene routine to prevent and manage dental issues.
- Orthodontics: Addressing bite issues and providing corrective appliances as needed.
- Vestibular rehabilitation: Addressing dizziness and balance issues.
- Genetic counseling: Discussing the implications of the ANKRD11 gene variant for future pregnancies and siblings.
- Vitamin D supplementation: Given the prevalence of vitamin D deficiency in affected individuals, considering supplementation to support bone health.
- Growth hormone therapy: Unlicensed for this condition but potentially beneficial in cases of short stature and delayed growth.
- Gluten-free diets: Considering dietary interventions for those with gluten sensitivity or celiac disease.
- Immunotherapy: Evaluating the benefits of immunomodulatory therapies for managing autoimmune manifestations and preventing infections.

    - Children with KBG syndrome may experience respiratory issues, including recurrent otitis media (middle ear infections) and temporary enlargement of the tonsils (tonsillar hypertrophy).

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are at increased risk of congenital heart defects, specifically abnormalities of the aortic valve and the pulmonary artery. These can lead to various cardiovascular issues, including heart murmurs, arrhythmias, and potential heart failure.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), leading to poor weight gain and nutritional deficiencies. They may also develop vitamin D deficiency rickets due to impaired calcium absorption.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Individuals with KBG syndrome are at increased risk of developing autoimmune diseases, particularly Type 1 diabetes mellitus and autoimmune thyroiditis. They are also more susceptible to fungal and viral infections.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome frequently exhibit developmental delays, behavioral differences, and learning difficulties. They may also display autistic-like behaviors, such as repetitive movements, difficulty with transitions between activities, and social awkwardness.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to otitis media (ear infections) and adenovirus-related encephalitis. They may also experience chronic sinusitis and allergic rhinitis.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Vision problems, including refractive errors (hypermetropia/hyperopia), astigmatism, and presbyopia (age-related near-sightedness), are common in KBG syndrome. Glaucoma is also a concern, potentially requiring early intervention.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Individuals with KBG syndrome are more prone to developing eczema and skin infections, particularly yeast infections (candidiasis). Frequent skin picking and irritations are also more common.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Teeth characteristics, such as macrodontia (large permanent teeth), brachydactyly (shortened fingers), and clinodactyly (curved fifth finger), are frequent in KBG syndrome. Orthodontic interventions may be necessary for bite alignment and tooth crowding.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Academic achievement can vary widely among individuals with KBG syndrome. While many receive mainstream education, those with significant learning difficulties may require additional support in the classroom. Special educational needs assessments (SEN assessments) and Individual Education Plans (IEPs) are crucial for managing learning challenges.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:

Parent: His front teeth are noticeably larger than they should be for a child of his age. The dentist says this could lead to some orthodontic issues later on if not addressed.

Parent: He was born with a septal defect. Fortunately, it's been managed well with regular check-ups and medication. So far‚ it hasn't held him back from playing or running around like other kids.

a) How this affects the patient:

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience respiratory issues, including recurrent otitis media (middle ear infections) and temporary blockage of the Eustachian tubes (glue ear). These can lead to hearing difficulties and temporary hearing loss, especially in young children.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular ENT (Ear, Nose, Throat) reviews for hearing concerns.
  - Monitoring for recurrent otitis media and glue ear.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of congenital heart defects, particularly valve abnormalities and atrial septal defects (ASDs). These can potentially lead to heart-related complications such as congestive heart failure, arrhythmias, and pulmonary hypertension.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular cardiac evaluations, including echocardiography and ECGs, to monitor for potential heart-related issues.
  - Follow-up care and management based on the specific heart-related concerns identified.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience feeding difficulties and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), leading to discomfort and poor appetite.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Addressing feeding difficulties through strategies such as modified bottle feeding techniques or tube feeding.
  - Treating GERD with dietary modifications and possible acid suppressants under medical supervision.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of developing autoimmune diseases, particularly Type 1 diabetes mellitus and thyroid disorders.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular screening for autoimmune markers and early intervention if autoimmune issues are identified.
  - Maintaining a healthy lifestyle and following immunization schedules recommended for the general population.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may exhibit developmental delays, behavioral differences, and learning difficulties.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Providing additional educational support and accommodations in school settings.
  - Implementing behavior management plans as needed.
  - Encouraging physical activity and social interaction to promote overall health and wellbeing.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are prone to recurrent otitis media (ear infections) and glue ear (build-up of fluid in the ear), which can lead to hearing difficulties and temporary hearing loss.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular ENT (Ear, Nose, Throat) reviews for hearing concerns.
  - Monitoring for recurrent otitis media and glue ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of vision problems such as astigmatism and short-sightedness (myopia).
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular eye checks to monitor vision and address any concerns promptly.
  - Ensuring proper hygiene practices to prevent bacterial conjunctivitis (pink eye).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may develop skin conditions such as eczema and keratosis pilaris, which can impact their self-esteem and willingness to participate in physical activities.
- Management Recommendations:

  - Encouraging open communication about feelings and concerns regarding their skin condition.

a) How this affects the patient:

- Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of tooth decay (dental caries) due to their enlarged permanent molars (large upper central incisors).

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Honestly, I'm getting a bit worried... she rubs her eyes a lot when she's trying to focus on something. It happens pretty often, and I've noticed it's been going on for a while now.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yeah... she asks me to repeat myself a lot. I mean, it's like she didn't quite catch what I said the first time around. It's happening more often than I'd like, to be honest.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: She's been complaing about sensitive teeth when she eats cold food. Like ice cream or cold water... it really bothers her. We've tried to get her to brush her teeth more regularly, but it's hard to get her into a routine.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: She gets tired really easily... more than other kids her age. Even after just playing for a little bit‚ she needs to sit down and rest. I worry it might be something serious.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves‚ muscle tone‚ fits).
Parent: There are these... episodes‚ I guess you'd call them‚ where she just stares off into space. It's really scary because she doesn't respond to me when it happens. I don't know what to do during those times.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding‚ stomach‚ bowel).
Parent: Bowel problems... yeah‚ that's been an issue. I'm not really sure what causes it‚ but it's been stressful dealing with.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: She has scoliosis... and hip dysplasia. The doctors have been monitoring both‚ and we go for regular check-ups to make sure everything's progressing as it should. It's a lot to take in‚ but I'm trying to stay on top of it all.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- None noted.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience respiratory issues, including recurrent ear infections and temporary loss of smell (anosmia). Proper hygiene practices and timely antibiotic treatment can reduce the frequency of these complications.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at risk of congenital heart defects, particularly valve abnormalities. Regular echocardiograms are recommended to monitor the heart and detect potential issues early.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). Management strategies such as gradual introduction of solid foods, dietary modifications, and antacid medications may be beneficial.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome are at increased risk of developing autoimmune diseases, particularly Type 1 diabetes and thyroid disorders. Regular screening and immunological assessments are advised.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Neurological features in KBG syndrome include developmental delays, behavioral differences, and sensorineural hearing loss. Management focuses on compensatory strategies and assistive devices.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are prone to recurrent otitis media and glue ear. Regular audiometric evaluations and consideration of hearing aid placement are essential.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Vision-related concerns in KBG syndrome include refractive errors, strabismus (eye misalignment), and possible optic nerve issues. Regular ophthalmologic examinations are crucial.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome may exhibit eczema-like skin conditions, particularly affecting the scalp and intertriginous areas. Gentle skincare routines and dermatologist consultations are advisable.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Dental issues in KBG syndrome include temporomandibular joint dysfunction, bruxism (teeth grinding), and susceptibility to cavities. Early orthodontic intervention and thorough oral hygiene practices are key.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Academic achievement in children with KBG syndrome can vary widely. While most receive mainstream education, accommodations such as extended breaks, simplified curriculum materials, and additional educational resources may be necessary.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- Behavioural differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety, are common. Parental support groups and therapeutic interventions can provide valuable support.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Research indicates that while most children with KBG syndrome achieve some level of academic success, the extent of educational attainment can vary greatly. Collaboration between educators, therapists, and families is critical for tailored support.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Skeletal characteristics, such as brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth finger), can impact physical activities requiring dexterity and flexibility. Orthopedic evaluation and guidance are recommended.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
### Screening Recommendations:
- **Referral for Cardiology Review**: Given the presence of heart conditions, regular cardiac evaluations are essential.
- **Referral for Vestibular Assessment**: Considering the unique gait and balance issues, a vestibular assessment might be beneficial.
- **Referral for Ophthalmology Review**: Frequent eye exams are necessary to address vision concerns and monitor for potential complications.

### Treatments Recommendations:
- **Orthodontics**: Addressing bite issues with braces or aligners.
- **Physical Therapy**: Enhancing mobility and reducing the effects of brachydactyly.
- **Occupational Therapy**: Supporting fine motor skills and adaptive techniques.
- **Speech Therapy**: Improving communication abilities and swallowing functions.
- **Behavioral Support**: Implementing strategies to manage behavioral differences and ASD traits.
- **Anti-Seizure Medications**: Managing seizure activity, particularly if frequent or resistant.
- **Antihistamines**: Treating allergic reactions and hay fever-like symptoms.
- **Vaccinations**: Ensuring adequate protection against infectious diseases, given the immune system’s compromised state.

This comprehensive approach addresses the multifaceted challenges faced by individuals with KBG syndrome, providing targeted interventions to optimize their quality of life and maximize functional outcomes. Regular reassessment and adaptation of care plans based on evolving needs are integral components of ongoing management.

Parent: Our daughter has hypermetropia, which means she has a higher than normal curvature of her eyeball. This affects how she sees things at close range and makes reading and focusing more difficult. She often squints when looking at books or toys up close.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes, our child gets easily frustrated in noisy environments. It's not that she can't hear well; it's just that the loud noises overwhelm her. In quieter settings, she responds appropriately to sounds and voices.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Her teeth have weak enamel. We have to ensure she brushes them carefully and regularly visits the dentist for check-ups to prevent any further issues. The dentist has also recommended a special toothpaste to help strengthen her teeth.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Due to a pre-existing condition, our child needs regular heart check-ups with a specialist. These check-ups monitor her heart health and ensure everything remains stable. So far‚ these have been routine and haven't indicated any major concerns.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain‚ nerves‚ muscle tone‚ fits).
Parent: Developmentally‚ she has been slower to reach certain milestones‚ such as walking or sitting unassisted. While she eventually achieves these milestones‚ it takes her longer than her peers. We work closely with physical therapists to support her development.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding‚ stomach‚ bowel).
Parent: Unfortunately‚ she experiences bowel problems. This includes constipation and occasional diarreah. Managing her diet and ensuring she stays hydrated helps alleviate these issues to some extent.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Besides the mentioned conditions‚ our child struggles with speech clarity. She finds it hard to express herself clearly‚ which can be frustrating for her. Additionally‚ she has a delayed fontanelle closure‚ where her soft palate doesn't move properly during speech‚ affecting her pronunciation. These are areas we're working on with speech therapists.

### Recommendations for Screening and Treatments

#### Vision
- Regular eye checks and orthokeratology lenses for near-sightedness.

#### Speech Therapy
- Continued speech therapy to address articulation and phonological delays.

#### Dental
- Regular dental check-ups and fluoride varnish application.

#### Behaviour Management
- Consultation with a behavior therapist for behavioral differences and ASD.

#### Orthodontics
- Monitoring of jaw development and potential orthodontic intervention.

#### Cardiology
- Follow-up appointments with cardiologist for ongoing cardiovascular assessments.

#### Neurology
- Ongoing neuropsychological evaluations and management of cognitive and behavioral challenges.

#### Immunology
- Routine vaccinations and consideration of additional immunomodulatory therapies.

#### Dentistry
- Regular dental cleanings and sealants for prevention of cavities.

#### Education
- Review of educational progress and potential accommodations based on current abilities.

#### Behaviour
- Implementation of behavior management strategies at home and in school.

#### Skeletal
- Regular X-rays of the hand and wrist to monitor bone age and assess for idiopathic scoliosis.

- Continue speech therapy for articulation and phonological delays.
- Schedule follow-up appointments with a behavior therapist for behavioral differences and ASD.
- Conduct periodic neuropsychological evaluations and cognitive assessments.
- Monitor jaw development and consider orthodontic interventions if necessary.
- Maintain regular follow-ups with the cardiologist for ongoing cardiovascular assessment.
- Encourage continued dental hygiene practices and schedule dental cleanings and sealants.
- Review educational progress and consider accommodations as needed.
- Monitor bone age and assess for idiopathic scoliosis through regular hand/wrist X-rays.
- Implement behavior management strategies at home and in school.
- Consider additional immunomodulatory therapies if standard vaccines fail to provide adequate protection.
- Maintain a consistent schedule of follow-up appointments with specialists as per the patient's evolving needs.

- Regular dental check-ups: Children with KBG syndrome should undergo regular dental examinations to address potential issues such as tooth decay and gum disease.

- Periodic orthopedic evaluations: X-rays of the wrists, hips, and spine should be taken periodically to assess bone density and rule out conditions such as scoliosis or developmental dyschondroblastoma.
- Audiologic evaluation: Routine audiometric testing should be conducted to identify hearing impairments early and initiate appropriate interventions.

- Speech therapy: Given the known speech delays, speech therapy should be considered as part of the standard care regimen.
- Behavioral therapy: Management strategies aimed at addressing behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, and anxiety, should be incorporated into the therapeutic plan.
- Nutritional support: Addressing feeding difficulties and ensuring adequate caloric intake should be a priority.
- Orthopedic intervention: Surgical correction of brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth digit) might be necessary depending on severity.
- Cardiac management: Regular follow-up with a pediatric cardiologist is essential to monitor for any ongoing heart conditions and ensure timely interventions.
- Vestibular rehabilitation: Considering vestibular therapy for children with KBG syndrome who exhibit balance or coordination challenges.

- Epilepsy management: Antiepileptic drugs should be considered for children with seizure history or susceptibility.
- Hormone replacement: Evaluation for growth hormone therapy should be considered in children with short stature and delayed physical maturation.
- Vitamin D supplementation: Due to the high prevalence of hearing loss and the importance of vitamin D in bone health, consideration should be given to vitamin D supplementation.
- Gluten-free diet: While not universally applicable, dietary restrictions based on gluten sensitivity or celiac disease should be evaluated in children with KBG syndrome.
- Dental hygiene: Implementing a comprehensive dental care routine tailored to the unique needs of KBG syndrome patients, including proper plaque control techniques and fluoride application protocols.
